description:
'''Alternative pop''' (also known as '''alt-pop''') is [[pop music]] with broad commercial appeal that is made by figures outside the mainstream, or which is considered more original, challenging, or eclectic than traditional pop music. The term has been used for a broad range of music and has described an artist's relationship to the musical mainstream as much as a single, fixed sound. The first known use of the term "alternative pop" recorded by ''[[Merriam-Webster]]'' dates to 1985, while the shortened term "alt-pop" is recorded from 1994.

''[[The Independent]]'' described alt-pop as "a home-made, personalized imitation of the mainstream that speaks far closer to actual teenage experience", and characterized one strand of the style as dark or downbeat, with lyrics addressing insecurity, regret, drugs, and anxiety. Historically, alternative pop has overlapped with [[alternative rock]], [[indie pop]], [[art pop]], [[electronic music]], and singer-songwriter traditions. In the 2010s and 2020s, artists associated with the term increasingly achieved mainstream commercial success, further blurring the distinction between alternative and mainstream pop.
